subject: Elastic retention credits & observability addon counterproposal
messages:
From: Mark Dawson <mark@atlasdata.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tina Li <tina.li@atlasdata.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability retention construct - initial ask

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the advanced dashboards look promising for our SRE team. Before we move to procurement, we need to align on the add-on pricing for retention and tracing. A few constraints from our side:

- Seasonal ingestion spikes (Q3) — want elasticity for retention without large overage surprises.
- Need a clear mapping: retention days -> monthly credits (so internal finance can model it).
- Want to understand how tracing samples interact with dashboard credits (are they separate buckets?).

Attached is a short export of our last quarter usage so you can see patterns (usage_breakdown_q1.csv). Can you propose a structure that keeps our GTM costs predictable and gives a path to scale credits?

If useful, procurement (procurement@atlasdata.com) should be looped for contract language once we have numbers.

Thanks — look forward to a simple model we can hand to finance.

Best,
Mark
VP, Platform Engineering
Atlas Data

Attachment: usage_breakdown_q1.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Mark Dawson <mark@atlasdata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability retention construct - initial ask

Thanks Mark — this is very helpful. I pulled together a short counterproposal to turn your usage into a predictable credit model and a fallback for spikes. See the attached pricing grid (redwood_observability_price_grid.xlsx). High level:

- Three-tier credit slabs (base / growth / surge) mapped to retention windows (7 / 30 / 90 days).
- Tracing samples billed as a separate metric with a bundled discount if you commit to the 30-day slab.
- Auto-burst buffer: small percentage of monthly credits reserved for short spikes; overage rate below typical market to avoid surprise invoices.

Suggested next steps:
1) Ben — can you validate the slab discounts and confirm expected margin impact?
2) Neha — can you confirm SLO/trace retention interaction (do we need to surface any migration caveats?)
3) Mark — if this looks directionally right, we can produce a SOW draft and send to procurement.

I attached the price grid and a redline-friendly SOW stub (atlas_sow_draft_v2.pdf). I kept the math simple so finance can plug in actual ingestion numbers.

Open to a 30-minute call this afternoon to walk through the grid.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_observability_price_grid.xlsx (Excel, 32KB); atlas_sow_draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 14KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability retention construct - initial ask

Looping in Rishi for the quant/ops view. Quick notes on the grid:

- Slab math looks reasonable; margin holds if Atlas commits to 12 months on the 30-day slab.
- Recommend changing the surge buffer from 10% -> 15% for Atlas specifically given their Q3 patterns in the CSV. That reduces overage frequency but increases committed credits slightly.
- For tracing: charge per sampled span, but offer a 20% bundle discount if they commit to both traces + dashboards in the same SOW.

If we move surge -> 15% we should explicitly call out a one-time re-score after 90 days to check usage drift.

-b

Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

(Attachment: redwood_observability_price_grid.xlsx — updated tab "surge-15pct")

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability retention construct - initial ask

Adding an operational note:

- Retention > 30 days requires enabling archival storage; pricing grid should call out readback cost for archived spans.
- For Atlas's use case, recommend a hybrid approach: keep hot 30 days, archive 31-90 with a lower read SLA. That lets them keep dashboards responsive while capping cost.
- We'll need to add a small migration fee if they later request rehydration of archived traces for e-discovery (~one-time).

I'll draft a short appendix for the SOW that defines hot vs archived behavior and the rehydration price. Once Ben confirms the surge % I'm happy to add it to the SOW PDF.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachment: appendix-archival-pricing.md (text stub referenced to be incorporated)

From: Mark Dawson <mark@atlasdata.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlasdata.com>, Tina Li <tina.li@atlasdata.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability retention construct - initial ask

Stephanie — thanks for the clear model. Atlas is comfortable with the 30-day base slab and the separate tracing metric, and we like the hybrid hot/archive approach Neha suggested. A few quick asks before we route to procurement:

- Can you set the surge buffer to 15% as Ben suggested and show a worked example for our Q3 projected spike in the price grid?
- Please add the rehydration one-time fee language to the SOW appendix.
- Can we have a clause for a single-score review at 90 days to rebaseline the credits?

If you can send an updated sheet and SOW tomorrow morning, we'll get procurement to start an internal PO review. Thanks — appreciate the speed on this.

Best,
Mark
VP, Platform Engineering
Atlas Data

Attachment referenced: atlas_sow_draft_v2.pdf (waiting updated appendix)
